editorial.headline: Conventional Banking Beyond Payments: KBLI 64123
editorial.standfirst: This conventional banking activity gathers public savings and extends credit, but does not provide payment-traffic services—and it remains open to PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 64123 covers conventional banking activity outside the general-banking system, including the model exemplified by a conventional Bank Perekonomian Rakyat. Its core work is clear but closely bounded: collecting funds from the public as deposits, savings, or comparable forms, then channeling those funds to the public as credit. The exclusion matters just as much as the inclusion. This activity does not provide services in payment traffic, including fund-transfer services. That is the line that gives the category its distinct character.

The activity is open at the Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. Across those scales, the record describes the same essential proposition: conventional banking based on gathering public funds in savings forms and extending credit, without entering the payment-services function. The result is a deliberately focused banking activity, defined by its deposit-and-credit role as well as by the services that sit outside its scope.

Nationally, the PMA position is straightforward. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, foreign ownership may reach 100% at the national level. The cited PMA basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower foreign-ownership cap in this record to soften or qualify that national position.

Bali does not reverse the national picture. The province’s permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities, but this activity is not blocked by that rule. Its Bali status is `OK_or_HIGHER_RISK`: at the Besar scale, the OSS risk is Medium-High/High, which is why it is outside the moratorium’s blocked category. For PMA registration, KBLI 64123 is therefore genuinely open in Bali today.
